name: Modern Defense
description: A hypermodern defense similar to the Pirc that teaches flexible counterplay and central pressure from distance.

branches.title: Main Line: g6 and Bg7
branches.description: Learn the default Modern setup against e4 and d4.

moves.title: White starts
moves.explanation: White takes space. e4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The Modern delays central contact while building pressure from g7; Black must strike before White rolls forward.

moves.title: Prepare bishop
moves.explanation: Black delays central pawns and prepares Bg7. g6 is a practical improving move for Black. In real games, keep asking: is my king safe, are my pieces active, and what central pawn break comes next?

moves.title: White expands
moves.explanation: White builds a strong center. d4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The Modern delays central contact while building pressure from g7; Black must strike before White rolls forward.

moves.title: Fianchetto
moves.explanation: Bg7 pressures the long diagonal and prepares flexible counterplay. Bg7 develops a bishop to g7. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Develop to c3

moves.title: Develop to e2
moves.explanation: Be2 improves a piece and adds control over important squares. Developed pieces create threats naturally, so you do not need to force an attack before castling.

hints: Follow the highlighted move and say the idea out loud.
After each move, check king safety, center control, and piece activity.
When a trade appears, ask what file opens and which piece improves next.

After the opening, do not drift: improve your worst piece, connect rooks, and look for one clear pawn break.
